prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Greenvale Metro CBTC (Communications-Based Train Control) System: separation, movement authority (MA), regulation. LTC declares degraded mode when MA, localization, points, platform interface or radio untrusted (loss of trust = loss of comms); trains stop or run at controlled speed. Return to automatic needs stable comms, verified routes, confirmed positions, recorded maintenance-to-operations handback; cybersecurity controls prerequisite. Safety-critical faults stay under traffic control until LTC and Maple confirm; evidence frozen; config versions recorded. Actors: Line Traffic Controller (LTC): monitors Lantern, no vital intervention; produces Temporary Speed Restriction Notice; receives Route Release Exception List; manual route recovery via independent indications/verbal reports; resets need LTC+Maple; notified when cyber event requires automatic-operation restriction or comms mode change. Revenue Train Operator: acknowledges to Atlas; restricted manual via Voice Dispatch Console; repeats back limit, speed, stopping point, platform-clear; sends Test Train Clearance Memo (Lantern uses it as prerequisite for security exceptions for non-revenue movement); no cyber admin in service; heeds cab security warnings. Signal Maintenance Engineer, alias Maple: read-only outside window; verifies points/vacancy before manual route; requests fault-isolation access. Cyber Security Officer: monitors security events from Safety Data Communication Network, Wayside Radio Access Network, Lantern; correlates auth failures, session resets, rejected messages, config changes, timing anomalies without altering safety paths; classifies alerts by impact, territory, MA effect; approves security-sensitive permissions; uses audit file for radio session continuity. Elements: Metro Operations Control System, alias Lantern: shows limits/fallback without obscuring alarms; sends Crew Login Token Bundle to Atlas. Maintenance Diagnostic Server, alias Quarry: read-only; checks Brake Curve Checksum Log; no cert bypass/alternate trust paths. North/South District Zone Controllers, aliases Marble/Orchid: send MA to Atlas; Marble applies speed restriction; Orchid inhibits auto routing under manual confirmation. East Junction Interlocking, alias Falcon: Axle Counter Reset Request; rejects messages with invalid signature, expired certificate, out-of-window sequence. West Junction Interlocking: sends Route Release Exception List to LTC. Interlockings final vital authority. Platform Screen Door Controller: Platform Door Status Snapshot. Atlas Onboard Controller, alias Kestrel: modes initialization, protected manual, ATO, fallback, cutout, restricted manual; produces Brake Curve Checksum Log. Train Radio Modem reports safe-data loss to Atlas. Cryptographic Key Management Appliance: sole certificate

New part:
S218: Audit records shall be protected from local alteration by the component that generates them and shall be retained for the period defined by Greenvale Metro governance.
S219: The Service Timetable Server and Passenger Information Gateway shall be monitored for compromise because incorrect operational context can influence control room decisions even when safety commands remain valid.
S220: The Voice Dispatch Console shall be included in security incident procedures when a cyber event changes the normal method for issuing operational instructions.
S221: The Platform Screen Door Controller shall accept only authenticated interfaces approved for passenger service coordination and maintenance testing.
S222: The Dual Channel Odometer and Atlas Onboard Controller shall report security-relevant diagnostic conditions in a manner that supports investigation without exposing cryptographic material.
S223: Security responsibilities shall be reviewed after major timetable changes, radio coverage modifications, control center upgrades, or any incident that questions the integrity of safety-related communications.
S224: Commissioning shall begin only after the installed equipment baseline for the Atlas Onboard Controller, Dual Channel Odometer, Train Radio Modem, and wayside control equipment has been configuration checked against the approved release record.
S225: The test-train phase shall use non-passenger movements to prove train localization, movement authority processing, braking response, radio continuity, and operator displays under controlled operating conditions.
S226: Each test train shall be crewed by a Revenue Train Operator qualified for commissioning duties and supported by a Line Traffic Controller with authority to stop the trial when observed conditions depart from the approved script.
S227: Initial movements shall be conducted at restricted commissioning speeds and shall progress to representative service speeds only after the Atlas Onboard Controller and North District Zone Controller demonstrate stable supervision.
S228: The South District Zone Controller shall be commissioned under the same test regime so that boundary behavior is verified before whole-line operation is attempted.
S229: East Junction Interlocking and West Junction Interlocking shall remain under enhanced monitoring during migration because route setting, point detection, and authority release behavior are critical to mixed-mode operation.
S230: The staged migration from legacy signalling shall divide the railway into controlled areas that can be commissioned, operated, and, if necessary, returned to legacy control without affecting uncommissioned areas.
S231: Cutover planning shall define the exact control boundaries, permissible train movements, staffing levels, and rollback conditions for each migration stage.
S232: Before any cutover stage, the Safety Data Communication Network and Wayside Radio Access Network shall be verified for coverage, latency, redundancy, and alarm presentation at the control center.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
